keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page names Danyang as capital and main base, Chang Prefecture, Wukang (where he was captured), Kuaiji (Shaoxing, the town he fled toward) and Mount Bowang (the Tang victory); the infobox says 'Zhejiang/Southern Jiangsu'. The Nanjing circle is the Tang dossier's own reading; the page gives no area.

region.text: Danyang (modern Nanjing), Chang Prefecture and the Jiangnan towns round it

ledger.note: 623: Fu Gongshi declares the Song. In the fall of 623 he 'rebels, claiming Li Fuwei was detained, and declares himself Emperor of Song' at Danyang, where he had been left in command in 622.

region.text: Zhang Shan'an's region: northern Jiangxi and eastern Hubei

ledger.note: 623: Zhang Shan'an submits. 'Zhang Shan'an submits to him' in the fall; the page places his region in northern Jiangxi and eastern Hubei.

region.text: Zhang Shan'an's region: northern Jiangxi and eastern Hubei

ledger.note: 623: Zhang Shan'an is captured. In the winter Li Daliang captured Zhang Shan'an.

region.text: Danyang (modern Nanjing), Chang Prefecture and the Jiangnan towns round it

ledger.note: 624: the Song falls. Li Xiaogong defeats Fu's generals at Mount Bowang; Fu 'flees Danyang, is captured' at Wukang and is executed by Li Xiaogong.

wars.name: Li Xiaogong's campaign against Fu Gongshi

zones.text: Danyang (modern Nanjing), Chang Prefecture and the Jiangnan towns round it

wars.outcome: Tang victory: Li Xiaogong beat Fu's generals at Mount Bowang in 624; Fu fled Danyang, was caught at Wukang and executed.

certainty.note: Rebel zone with no frontier on the page.

sources.title: Fu Gongshi

notes: Written for ea-04-x (listed by ea-03-f and the Tang dossier as 'Fu Gongshi (Song)'; no Cliopatria row). The Tang dossier's only event is the 624 gain; it has no 623 loss. The page does not support the 619 proclamation or a 621 submission that the earlier reports assumed: Fu and Du Fuwei were Tang's Duke of Shu and Prince of Wu from summer 620. Zhang Shan'an has no dossier (name only). The regions are circles, not frontiers.
